free_tier.stated: free IPv6 tunnel with a routed /56 subnet over WireGuard, GRE, IP6IP, SIT, GRETAP, VXLAN or L2TPv3, self-service

per_object_cap.stated: a routed /56 per tunnel endpoint, stated on the home page as 'IPv6 tunnels with a routed /56 subnet'

retention.stated: static IP allocations are stated to remain permanently assigned to the account; the portal was not opened, so what inactivity does to an allocation was not established

egress.terms: free transit up to 200 Mbit/s, traffic not metered, more available on request or by donation

interface_detail: a self-service web portal that issues tunnel configs; not a machine, so there is no shell of its own
tooling: the portal generates WireGuard configuration; any client can terminate the other end
chaining: an IPv6 address space and a WireGuard peer for a machine that has no IPv6 of its own, which is a routing service and not a host

limits.value: up to 200 Mbit/s on the free transit
no byte quota: 'Traffic is not metered'

binding_note: 200 Mbit/s is the only published ceiling; there is no traffic meter, so throughput is the constraint and volume is not.

identity_cost.detail: the portal is described as self-service and fully automated; the registration form was not read, so whether an email address alone suffices is unverified.

reliability_note: no SLA is stated on the home page; the service is donation-funded
confidence_note: the /56, the protocol list and the 200 Mbit/s cap are quoted from the home page read today

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Route64 provides IPv6 tunnels with a routed /56 subnet, delivered through multiple tunnel protocols (WireGuard, GRE, IP6IP, etc.) to your endpoint.'
quoted: 'Get free IPv4 / IPv6 transit for your network to bring your IP prefixes to the DFZ with up to 200M. Traffic is not metered'
quoted: 'Static IP allocations that remain permanently assigned to your account.'
route64.com is a parked domain listed for sale; a request for route64.com redirected to the GoDaddy for-sale page, so the provider is route64.org and the .com is not it

notes: This is not a machine and cannot be one: it gives an address and a peer, and the client still needs something to terminate the tunnel on. It is recorded because it is the way an IPv6-only or CGNAT machine acquires a routable prefix. the terms were not read by us, so that is reported and not verified. The egress topic owns the tunnel; this record covers only the address space.
